[Thinking]
**Evaluating CPT codes**

I’m working on recommending CPT codes for a procedure involving ALIF at the L5-S1 level. I think 22558 is the right choice for that. For anterior instrumentation, I’m considering 22845, but it covers two to three segments, so maybe 22842 for a single level? For removing an implant, I’m not sure if 22849 or 22855 is more appropriate. I should suggest 22558 and 76000 for localization, while advising the coder to consult the operative report and CPT manual for clarity.
[/Thinking]

Summary recommendation and rationale — please verify with your facility/coding guidance and payer rules (operative report is needed for final coding). Based on the operative description, the dominant billed procedure is an anterior lumbar interbody fusion at L5–S1 with removal of a previously placed posterior TLIF interbody device and placement of an anterior interbody (4WEB ring) plus anterior instrumentation. Fluoroscopy was also used for localization.

Likely CPT codes to consider (start here and confirm with local coding resources and the full op note):

1) 22558 — Arthrodesis, anterior interbody technique, including disc space preparation, discectomy, and placement of interbody device and bone graft, single interspace, lumbar — This code is appropriate for an anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) at a single level (L5–S1) that includes insertion of an interbody device and graft material. Use this as the primary fusion code.

2) 22845 (or alternative anterior instrumentation code) — Instrumentation for spinal fusion, anterior approach (buttress plate with screws) — There are several instrumentation codes depending on number of levels and specific hardware; 22845 is commonly used for anterior instrumentation spanning multiple levels (refer to CPT text to choose the exact code that matches the number of vertebral segments instrumented and the device type). Review the CPT descriptors to select the exact anterior instrumentation code that matches the plate/screw construct used.

3) Code(s) for removal of prior interbody device (revision) — Removal of previously implanted interbody/implant may be separately reportable. There is not a single universally used code for “removal of interbody cage” in all situations; possible relevant codes include removal/revision of spinal implants (e.g., 22830 for removal of posterior segmental instrumentation or other implant removal codes). You must review the specific CPT descriptors and the surgeon’s documentation of removal/revision to determine the correct implant removal/revision code. If the removal was performed as part of the same operative field and included as part of the interbody fusion, some payers consider it inclusive — verify payer policy.

4) 76000 or intraoperative fluoroscopy guidance code — 76000 is “fluoroscopic guidance for needle placement” (commonly used for simple fluoroscopic localization), but intraoperative fluoroscopy for localization or imaging during the procedure may instead be reported with 77003 or other imaging guidance codes per facility policy. Many coders report a fluoroscopic localization code when fluoroscopy was used solely for localization; check local billing policy and whether facility or C-arm use is billed separately.

Modifiers and other notes:
- Use appropriate modifiers for bilateral or multiple procedures if required.
- If removal of the posterior TLIF cage was performed through a separate approach or represents a distinct procedure, you may report removal/revision codes in addition to the ALIF code; if removal is incidental to the ALIF and payer policy disallows separate reporting, do not bill separately.
- Facility (hospital) coding and physician professional component vs technical component distinctions: make sure imaging guidance is billed correctly (global/professional/technical).
- ICD-10 diagnosis codes should support the medical necessity (e.g., Lumbosacral spondylosis with radiculopathy, pseudarthrosis, loosening or malposition of prior fusion hardware if applicable).

Recommendation: Have your certified coder review the complete operative report and intraoperative notes and cross-check these suggested codes against the current CPT manual and payer-specific rules. If you want, provide the full operative report and I will map more precisely to exact CPT codes (including instrumentation and implant removal codes and suggested modifiers).
